contradictions.what: Rep says nothing bombed and it was a good cycle, yet no customer-specific value was shown and offered analysis was declined.
Rep says price match 'Yes. Probably.' then 'maybe not only the rate', then flatly 'we win this' with more rate room.
Rep said Lucy was sold and no figure was needed, but admits Martin saw nothing from us on the cost of failures.
Rep says 'same thing' isn't true and comparison unfair, yet attributes loss to rate rather than our failure to show the difference.
Lucy called it a formality shortly before Martin rejected it; the champion's read was wrong.
Martin is named decider but rep never met him; Lucy presented and the rep assumes what Lucy told him.
Martin's quoted line appears in two wordings: 'not going to pay more for the same thing' vs 'Why would I pay more for the same thing.'

dodges.question: Which part of our pitch got a reaction, and which got silence?
dodges.what: Named only positives, said 'Silence, honestly, nothing bombed', and skipped to the loss reason; no silent section identified.

dodges.question: Did we put a figure on the value they'd get? A figure for Fernbrook.
dodges.what: Initially answered with the generic uplift slide; only admitted no customer figure when pressed, and justified skipping the offered analysis.

dodges.question: So what did Martin have in front of him about what one in twelve orders was costing?
dodges.what: Answered 'Nothing from us' after a pause, then assumed Lucy told him.

dodges.question: If we had matched the price, would we have won? What else would have needed to be true?
dodges.what: Said yes, then listed other obstacles, then reverted to 'rate is what killed it'.
